topic: Who was responsible for stealing the briefcase: Porter 2 or Porter 3?

turns.speaker: A
turns.utterance: A group of porters was assigned to serve first-class passengers on the train journey that included Ed Beatty. During this trip, Ed discovered that his briefcase was missing from his cabin, leading to an investigation about which porter might have taken it. Around noon on the day in question, Porter 2, who was described as a distinguished looking man of perhaps forty, knocked on Ed’s door to announce that the dining room was open [E15]. Ed privately thought that Porter 2 seemed much too elegant to be a porter on a train, although he considered that the railroad might assign its best staff to first-class travelers [E16]. Porter 2 was noted for his impeccable manners, having assisted Porter 1 in welcoming Ed earlier that day and apologizing for momentarily forgetting Ed’s name [E17]. Later that evening, Porter 3 came on duty; he appeared to be about forty-five years old and was less friendly than the other porters, coming across as slightly standoffish, though he remained cordial and polite [E22]. At that time, Ed noticed that Porter 3’s uniform was especially well-fitted and freshly pressed, possibly because he had just started his shift [E23]. These events and observations were central to the circumstances surrounding the disappearance of Ed’s briefcase.
turns.content_fidelity_note: All required facts were included in chronological order, following the assigned content goal.

turns.utterance: On a cross-country train journey, Ed Beatty was traveling in a first class sleeper car that was serviced by several porters throughout the day. During this trip, Ed discovered that his briefcase, which held important personal papers and a foreign passport, had gone missing from his cabin. Earlier in the day, Porter 2 had assisted Porter 1 in welcoming Ed, displaying impeccable manners and apologizing when he momentarily forgot Ed’s name [E17]. That evening, Porter 3 came on duty. Porter 3 was observed to be about forty-five years old and, unlike the other porters, was not especially friendly; he was slightly standoffish, though he remained cordial, greeting Ed with a tip of his cap and formally informing him that the dining car was open [E22]. At that time, Ed also noticed that Porter 3’s uniform appeared particularly well-fitted and freshly pressed, perhaps because he had just started his shift [E23]. These interactions and observations occurred before Ed later realized his briefcase was missing from his room.
